Heatmap of protein expression

Source: R/plot_heatmap.R
plot_heatmap.Rd

Creates a clustered heatmap of protein expression values. Accepts data in long format (pivots to wide internally), already in wide format, or an OlinkExperiment object.

Usage

plot_heatmap(
  data,
  assay_col = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  sample_col = NULL,
  wide = NULL,
  annotation_cols = NULL,
  annotation_rows = NULL,
  pathway_annotation = FALSE,
  scale = "row",
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  show_rownames = FALSE,
  show_colnames = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  fontsize = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  as_ggplot = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or OlinkExperiment. Long format must have `assay_col`, `value_col`, and `sample_col`. Wide format should have samples as rows and proteins as columns.

assay_col

Name of the assay column (long format). If NULL, auto-detected (e.g. "Assay").

value_col

Name of the NPX value column (long format). If NULL, auto-detected (e.g. "NPX").

sample_col

Name of the sample ID column. If NULL, auto-detected (e.g. "SampleID" or "SubjectID").

wide

If TRUE, data is assumed to be in wide format. If NULL (default), format is detected automatically: wide when no assay/value columns are found.

annotation_cols

Columns to use for column (sample) annotation tracks. If NULL and data is an OlinkExperiment, the sample covariates in colData() are shown automatically (sample-id and constant/technical columns are excluded). Pass a character vector to select or override specific covariates.

annotation_rows

Columns to use for row (biomarker) annotation tracks that group the proteins into sets (e.g. the Olink Panel a protein belongs to). If NULL and data is an OlinkExperiment, the protein-level columns in rowData() are shown automatically (assay/id and constant columns are excluded). Pass a character vector to select specific columns.

pathway_annotation

Logical or data.frame: when TRUE, the biomarkers are grouped into a Pathway row annotation by running pathway enrichment with enrich_pathways() (requires gprofiler2 and an internet connection). Alternatively, pass a precomputed protein -> pathway data.frame with Protein and Pathway columns (each protein is annotated with its top pathway). Default FALSE (no pathway annotation).

scale

Scaling direction: "row", "column", or "none" (default "row").

cluster_rows

Logical; perform hierarchical clustering on rows (default TRUE). With more than 100 rows the row dendrogram is not drawn (rows are still ordered by the clustering) unless you pass `treeheight_row`.

cluster_cols

Logical; perform hierarchical clustering on columns (default TRUE).

show_rownames

Logical; show row (protein) names (default FALSE, usually too many).

show_colnames

Logical; show column (sample) names. If NULL (default), names are shown when there are at most 100 columns; in journal-size mode (`options(olinkviz.base_size)` below 11) at most `30 * 7 / base_size`, i.e. 30 at 7 pt; more labels than that cannot be read and collide.

color

Palette of colors for the heatmap gradient.

fontsize

Base font size in points. If NULL (default), 8; in journal-size mode (`options(olinkviz.base_size)` below 11) the tick-label size, `base_size - 1`.

main, title

Title for the heatmap.

as_ggplot

Logical; if `TRUE`, wraps the `pheatmap` gtable into a `patchwork`/`ggplot` element (requires `patchwork`) so it can be combined into multi-panel figures with `+` or `/` (default `FALSE`).

...

Additional arguments passed to `pheatmap::pheatmap()`.

Value

A `pheatmap` object (invisibly), or a `patchwork`/`ggplot` object when `as_ggplot = TRUE`.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Long format: column names are detected automatically
plot_heatmap(beatmg_npx, annotation_cols = "Timepoint")

# Wide format: detected automatically, no pivoting arguments needed
plot_heatmap(pcnsl_olink)
} # }
